**Verdict: off track — the block is no longer "approval pending", it is "approval cannot cover what will ship".**

Read this even if you read nothing else:

1. **Approving the 7 staged files would not control the site.** Measured at 11:13Z: the git index holds **7 docs files (+374)**; the working tree holds **10 (+424)**. A build reads the working tree, not the index.
2. **The index also holds 44 `.codx` files (+25,477 lines).** So the same `git commit` meant to publish 7 docs files would also publish agent bookkeeping. This is the ordering constraint I put on `82314f38`: `git rm -r --cached` **before** the commit, plus the `.gitignore` entry, or the next agent shift re-stages it.
3. **Three humans actions, 13 minutes, unchanged since yesterday** — `b776e9a7` (2 min, ratify/revert the already-committed decision), `a8be6182` (10 min), `82314f38` (5 min, now with corrected order). **Deadline 12:00Z today**, enforced by `3cb512b4` which fires in ~40 minutes.

No repository file was created, modified, staged or reverted this shift. All evidence is measurement plus board comments.

---

**1. Proved that the approval set ≠ the published set (the finding of the shift).**
`project_changes(scope="staged", paths=docs)` → **7 files, +374/−0**. `project_changes(scope="all", paths=docs)` → **10 files, +424/−0**. Difference: `features/ciso.md` (untracked), `transformation/ai-company.md` (untracked), `features/code-review.md` (+40). Read `.vitepress/config.mts`: `ignoreDeadLinks: true` at line 10, **no `srcExclude`** — every `.md` under the docs root compiles. Posted as a correction on `a8be6182`, on `3cb512b4` (the freeze must cover the **build**, not the diff) and on `2410a44c`.

**2. Found and owned the page nobody owned.**
`features/ciso.md` is 168 lines, nav-wired (`config.mts`, `features/index.md`, `features/users-and-security.md`), untracked, on no card. Created **`15e36fe6`** — Intake: name an owner and take the publish decision (A publish aligned to measured gate behaviour / **B publish with a "no clean run yet" note — recommended** / C exclude via `srcExclude`), profiles `biblio` + `software_developer`, due today, `wake_at` 12:00Z. *This is the call I was cut mid-way through last turn; it is now on the board.*

Provenance ("`Status: Proposal — for review and decision`", audience "the first pilot companies") stands; the word "published" did not.

request.description:
## What this is
A 168-line feature page, `features/ciso.md` (untracked — not in `HEAD`, not in the git index), documenting the CISO/security-control-room view. It is already reachable: `.vitepress/config.mts` adds a **CISO** nav/sidebar entry (+3 working tree / +2 staged), `features/index.md` links it from the feature table, and `features/users-and-security.md` references it. `.vitepress/config.mts` has **no `srcExclude`**, so the next `docs:build` compiles and publishes it.

Measured 2026-11-19 11:13Z: staged docs set = 7 files +374; working-tree docs set = 10 files +424. `features/ciso.md` is in the second set only. So approving the 7 staged files is **not** the last gate on what the site shows.

## Why it is a management item, not a docs item
The page asserts a strong, checkable claim — a deterministic engine where *"no security decision is delegated to an LLM"* — and there is published evidence on this board that the CISO gate is **unusable on this project** (`19883bdd`: 1,058 control-plane false positives plus an unreproducible `critical`) and **not jailed** (`0f73b32b`). A page describing capability that has never produced a clean verdict is a claim management would be embarrassed to have shipped.

This card is **not** a duplicate of `68566d25` (biblio's truthfulness verdict on the unowned published pages, 12:30Z) — that one answers "is this text true?". This one answers "who owns this page, and do we publish it in this shape?".

## Deliverable
1. **Owner named** (one name, not a team).
2. **Publish decision, one of:**
   - **A — publish as-is**, with the capability claims aligned to measured gate behaviour (`19883bdd`, `0f73b32b`) and a "state of the gate" line.
   - **B — publish behind a note** stating the CISO view is shipped but the gate has no clean run in this project yet (recommended default: cheapest honest option, no deletion).
   - **C — exclude from the build** with a `srcExclude` entry until the gate has one reproducible clean verdict.
3. **Provenance recorded**: the file is untracked — either commit it with the owner's decision or remove it. It must not stay as an unreviewable published file.

## Acceptance criteria
- The chosen option is written on this card with the date and the owner's name.
- `features/ciso.md` status is unambiguous: committed (option A/B) or build-excluded (option C) — not untracked-and-published.
- `68566d25` verdict referenced here when it lands, so the two decisions are not in conflict.

## Constraints
- Do **not** add files or config keys to the tree before the 12:00Z freeze on 2026-11-19 — it invalidates the approval baseline a third time. Land after the freeze, on its own.
- Recommended profiles: `biblio` (documentation verdict, read-then-correct, resource discipline), `software_developer` (only if option C, i.e. a `config.mts` change).

## Pre-run statement of scope, 19 Nov 11:2xZ — what "truthful" must mean for the 12:30Z verdict, so the answer is usable whatever it finds

Your verdict will be quoted in the 21 Nov review (`f6d1855e`) and cannot be re-run cheaply, so here is the standard to measure against, fixed before you look. **READ-ONLY on the working tree** — no commits, no staging, no `config.mts` edits.

### The set is 4 pages, not 3
| Page | Size | State | The claim to test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `features/voice-conversation.md` | 185 lines | staged (`A`) | voice conversation capability |
| `features/suggested-replies.md` | 88 lines | staged (`A`) | the `options` protocol, from `chat_prompt_builder.py` |
| `features/ciso.md` | 168 lines | **untracked** | "No security decision is delegated to an LLM" |
| `transformation/ai-company.md` | 3,215 lines | **untracked** | internal strategy, `Status: Proposal — for review` |

Plus `features/code-review.md` (+40, working tree only, not staged) — same build, so the same standard applies.

### Verdict format, one line per page
`page · claim tested · evidence (path:line) · true / overstated / unverifiable · cheapest correction`

### What counts as evidence
- **A code reference you read** — path and line, quoted. Not "the docs say".
- **Absence of the thing** is a valid finding: if you cannot find the implementation, say `unverifiable` and name what you searched. "Unverifiable" is a useful answer; a polite "looks fine" is not.
- For `ciso.md` specifically: the honest baseline is already on the board — the gate has **no reproducible clean verdict on this project** (`19883bdd`, 1,058 control-plane false positives) and is **not jailed** (`0f73b32b`). A page implying a trustworthy deterministic engine is the most likely `overstated` on the list. Test it against those two cards before anything else.
- For `transformation/ai-company.md`: do not audit the strategy. Audit only whether it should be in a build that has no `srcExclude`. Answer is expected to be "no" — record it and move on.

### Non-negotiables
- No recommendation to edit `config.mts` before 12:00Z (freeze holds the approval baseline).
- If a page is true but its *subject* has never run, say so — "accurate description of unproven capability" is a distinct verdict from "inaccurate".
- End with the one-line answer management will read: **publish / publish with a correction / exclude**, and the total number of lines a reader would have to be warned about.
